why_this_file_exists: The prefix holds the whole country twice per edition: one object per province and one per district, and the object names (30563-N.zip) say nothing about which is which. Loading both would double every parcel. The district set is the one to load, because it is the finer grain and it is what silver.parcel_boundaries already holds. The provider reuses file numbers across editions, so an object name alone does not say which edition it is either: the shapefile inside does. This file holds the rules that read that; which objects hold an edition is a fact of the Bronze ledger (catalog.bronze_object and the ZIP members measured beside it, root ADR-0169 §1), derived at run time by the publisher's vworld-parcel-editions command. Until 2026-10 every edition's 272 objects were listed here by hand, one pull request per edition (root ADR-0224).
member_name_reason: An object belongs to an edition when exactly one of its ZIP members matches: the edition is the provider base month in the shapefile name, the region its code — two digits a province object, five a district object.
consistency_check: The leading two digits of an edition's district codes cover every province code of its province objects, which is what makes them two coverings of one country rather than two different datasets. An edition where this does not hold is skipped as a partial collection.
snapshot_id_reason: An edition loads into silver.parcel_boundaries as source_snapshot_id = snapshot_id_prefix + edition, and valid_from_utc = the first instant of its provider base month (vworld_parcel_editions.py). Both were typed by hand per run, which is how the same June data was written as vworldkr__parcel-202606 and the September data as vworldkr__parcel:202609 (root ADR-0131, ADR-0148).

new_edition_bounds.$comment: How far a proposed edition may differ from the edition before it before it is skipped as a partial collection (vworld_parcel_source_contract::editions, root ADR-0148 §6, ADR-0224). Its 시군구 objects must cover the previous edition's 시도, except where 시도 merge: a 시도 may leave only while another appears, and at most max_sido_set_difference 시도 codes may differ in all (2026-07: 29 and 46 left, 12 appeared, 3). Its 시군구 count may differ by at most max_sigungu_count_change_share of the previous count (202606 → 202609: 255 → 256). A half-updated provider listing fails both.

served_edition_reason: The edition the map, the parcel catalog projection, the PostGIS mirror, the parcel panel Gold and the 시군구 crosswalk's cadastral 시도 are built from. Other editions are evidence (the legal-dong pairing reads two of them) until a reviewed change moves this value.
served_edition_sido_reason: The 시도 the served edition's district objects cover: the cadastral set the 시군구 crosswalk is compiled against (root ADR-0142). It moves with served_edition in the same reviewed change; every ledger read refuses a ledger whose served edition covers other 시도.
handoff_suffix_reason: The converter names the object and the loader must derive the same name, so the suffix is here rather than spelled in both scripts. `.gz` also tells the converter to compress and tells Spark to decompress — one string decides both, because two would eventually disagree and produce a file the reader cannot open. Measured 2026-08-31: gzip leaves 20% of a 625 MB national parcel handoff, and the conversion is bound by wire speed.
handoff_prefix_reason: Where the converted handoff objects live: an edition's are under handoff_prefix + /edition=<edition>. It was a default in three callers — the exporter that writes them, the batch loader that reads them, and the catalog projection command — so renaming the prefix meant editing three files and any one of them missed would have looked in a place nothing was written to. Each edition has its own: 202609 handoffs written on 2026-09-27 by hand under the 202606 prefix carry another snapshot id, and a loader that found them there would skip the conversion and load them. handoff_prefix_legacy keeps the prefix of the edition loaded before the per-edition rule; it is closed.
